name: HV 12202
description: A Cepheid in the Large Magellanic Cloud that pulsates every 3.10 days; its mean radius is 21.7 solar radii.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 12202: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 21.7 +/- 1.4 (Monte-Carlo)

temperature.source: Groenewegen & Lub (2023), A&A 676, A136, VizieR J/A+A/676/A136/table1, Name=LMC4646, columns Teffp, e_Teffp: Teff 5625 +/- 277 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic)

radialVelocity.source: No catalogued radial velocity: Gaia DR3 measures none for source 4663635851217102976 and SIMBAD lists none. Zero is assumed; a 30 km/s error moves the star by one part in 10,000,000 of its distance per century

distance.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 12202: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 35765.2 +/- 2234.2 (Monte-Carlo)

color.reason: Interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 0.06 +/- 0.005 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation

text.card: A Cepheid in the Large Magellanic Cloud, 22 times the Sun's width, that swells and shrinks every 3.1 days.
text.introduction: Its mean radius, 21.7 solar radii, comes from comparing how fast its surface moves with how its size changes, 35,765 parsecs away.

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius.
No dynamical mass is measured for this Cepheid; its mass is left unmeasured.
No surface gravity averaged over the pulsation is published, only single-phase values, so no limb darkening is drawn.
Its distance is the Baade-Wesselink one its radius was measured at, so the Magellanic Cepheids spread a few kiloparsecs in depth.
